segments: And two months after he began to reign,
he was deposed from the kingdom in Damascus,
and he went into hiding.
And his whereabouts were not known for five years;
and he was found in a battle of the Arabs with one another among the slain.
Now this Ibrahim was called 'the Ass of the Jazira',
because he loved the saffron rose,
which is called 'the wild rose' (or 'ass's rose',
or 'wine-colored rose'),
— this he loved.
And his entire time he held sway over the Jazira of Qardu.
Then he went out from Armenia and met Sulayman near the banks of the Euphrates,
and twelve thousand of his men were killed,
and he fled to al-Rusafa.
And Marwan came to Damascus,
and reigned in it for two months.
And he took the royal treasures, as much as a load of three thousand camels,
and he came and encamped against Homs.
And after four months he captured it,
and demolished its wall,
and crushed its hewn stones with sledgehammers.
And he also demolished the wall of Baalbek.
And he came to Harran,
and went down towards Assyria,
and to the land of Parthia, which is Isfahan.
Then Abu'l-Abbas—
who was Abdallah, son of Muhammad, son of Ali, son of Abdallah, son of Abbas, the uncle of the prophet of the Muslims—
with a large army of the Khurasanians, encamped on the Zab (Zaba) River in Assyria.
And Marwan came and met the army of Abu'l-Abbas,
and Marwan was defeated.
And seven hundred camel-loads of gold and silver were plundered from him.
And he, along with his son and his son-in-law, came in shame to Harran,
and loaded his treasures on three thousand camels, and went to Ascalon on the seacoast.
And Abu'l-Abbas pursued after him,
and he fled towards Aswan, a city on the border of the Nubians.
And while he was encamped on the banks of the Nile, he was overtaken and killed.
At this time, there went out from Constantinople Artabasdos {OCR?}, the commander of the Armeniacs, and came against Melitene,
and plundered the entire region.
And the Emperor Constantine, having defeated the tyrant Artabasdos,
prospered in the kingdom.
And a son was born to him by the daughter of the Khagan,
and he was named Leo.
And the lands of the Romans were at peace,
because the Arabs were plunged into internal wars with one another.
